blocking_question: The T038 contract pins the second-pool PoolId as `0xEd50bDeeA8aDC232f159486192a4157281D722ff`, which is 40 hex chars (20 bytes, address-sized). The V4 PoolId is keccak256(abi.encode(PoolKey)), which is 32 bytes / 64 hex chars; the offline re-derivation check cannot produce a 20-byte output by construction. Is the pinned identifier intentionally an EVM address rather than a V4 PoolId, or should it be replaced with the canonical 32-byte keccak256 digest of the resolved second-pool PoolKey? If the address-sized identifier is correct, please supply the 32-byte PoolId alongside so the resolver can re-derive against the correct pinned value. triage_request.observed_problem: T038 contract pins the second pool's PoolId as `0xEd50bDeeA8aDC232f159486192a4157281D722ff`, which is 40 hex chars / 20 bytes / 160 bits. A V4 PoolId is keccak256(abi.encode(PoolKey)) and must therefore be 32 bytes / 64 hex chars / 256 bits. The T038 must-not forbids guessing the PoolKey from the PoolId, so the resolver must re-derive the PoolId from the resolved PoolKey and compare against the pinned value; the re-derivation cannot produce a 20-byte output by construction. The contract says the run halts when the keccak256 check disagrees; the resolver returns `resolve_pinned_pool_id_size_defect` with an explicit error_detail, but the contract itself is the inconsistency.
